\worksheethead

\vspace{4pt}

\begin{keyf}
\textbf{Key formulas.} The $n$th Taylor polynomial for $f$ about $x = x_0$ and the $n$th Maclaurin polynomial ($x_0 = 0$) are
$$p_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{f^{(k)}(x_0)}{k!}(x - x_0)^k, \qquad p_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{f^{(k)}(0)}{k!}x^k.$$
\end{keyf}

\vspace{6pt}

\typehead{Type A: First Few Taylor Polynomials About $x_0$}{Make a table of $f^{(k)}(x)$ and $f^{(k)}(x_0)$, then substitute into the Taylor formula one term at a time.}

\begin{sample}{Find the first four Taylor polynomials for $e^x$ about $x = 1$.}
Every derivative of $e^x$ is $e^x$, so $f(1) = f'(1) = f''(1) = f'''(1) = e$.
\vspace{-4pt}
\begin{align*}
p_0(x) &= e, \qquad p_1(x) = e + e(x-1), \qquad p_2(x) = e + e(x-1) + \tfrac{e}{2!}(x-1)^2,\\
p_3(x) &= e + e(x-1) + \tfrac{e}{2}(x-1)^2 + \tfrac{e}{6}(x-1)^3.
\end{align*}
\end{sample}
